attractions.name: Le Morne Brabant
attractions.desc: A dramatic basalt mountain rising sharply from the island's southwest coast, listed by UNESCO for its history as a refuge for escaped slaves. The surrounding lagoon is also home to a famous optical illusion, an underwater 'waterfall' visible from the air where sand slopes drop off the shelf. It's one of the most photographed views in the country.

attractions.name: Chamarel Seven Coloured Earths
attractions.desc: A small geological site where volcanic soil has settled into distinct bands of red, brown, and purple that never mix, even after rain. It sits near a striking waterfall of the same name and a well-known rum distillery. The combination makes for an easy half-day trip inland from the coast.

attractions.name: Black River Gorges National Park
attractions.desc: The island's largest area of native forest, laced with hiking trails through steep gorges and past several waterfalls. It's one of the few places to see Mauritius's endemic birds, several of which were brought back from the edge of extinction. Trails range from easy viewpoints to full-day hikes.

attractions.name: Île aux Cerfs
attractions.desc: A small island off the east coast reached only by boat, ringed by turquoise water and white sand beaches. It's set up for a full day of swimming, water sports, and a round of golf on its course. Boat trips there often stop at a waterfall on the way.

attractions.name: Port Louis Central Market
attractions.desc: The capital's covered market is the best place to see the island's cultural mix up close, from spice stalls to Creole street food. Nearby, the Caudan Waterfront adds a more polished harborside shopping and dining area. It's a useful stop for a sense of daily life beyond the resorts.

attractions.name: Grand Bassin
attractions.desc: A crater lake considered one of the holiest Hindu sites outside India, ringed by temples and a towering statue of Shiva visible from the road below. It draws large pilgrimage crowds during the Maha Shivaratri festival but is quiet and contemplative most other days. The setting, in the island's forested highlands, adds to its atmosphere.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: South coast & Le Morne
itinerary.desc: Settle in near Le Morne, with time for the lagoon and coastal views.
itinerary.cost: Beach access is generally free; kitesurfing lessons run €40–60/hour given the area's strong winds.
itinerary.food: Try a fresh fish curry at a beachfront restaurant — a genuine reflection of the island's Creole cooking.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Chamarel & Black River Gorges
itinerary.desc: The coloured earths, a waterfall, and a hike through native forest.
itinerary.cost: The Seven Coloured Earths site costs about MUR 150; the waterfall viewpoint is free nearby.
itinerary.food: Try rougaille at a local restaurant near Chamarel, often made with fresh-caught fish.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Grand Bassin
itinerary.desc: A cultural detour inland to the sacred crater lake.
itinerary.cost: Entry to the site is free, though a small donation is customary.
itinerary.food: Street food stalls near the lake sell dholl puri, a good, cheap on-the-go option.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: East coast & Île aux Cerfs
itinerary.desc: Beach time and a boat trip out to the small offshore island.
itinerary.cost: A boat trip to Île aux Cerfs costs about €25–40 round trip, sometimes including a barbecue lunch.
itinerary.food: A beach barbecue lunch on Île aux Cerfs, often bundled with the boat trip, is a genuine highlight of this stop.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Port Louis
itinerary.desc: The capital's market and waterfront before departure.
itinerary.cost: The Central Market is free to wander; a few souvenirs and spices make reasonably priced take-home options.
itinerary.food: Try mine frite from a stall in the market, reflecting the island's Chinese-Mauritian influence.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% is appreciated but not obligatory; many resorts add a service charge already
goodToKnow.safety: Very safe for visitors, including for solo travelers and families
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Rental cars and taxis both work well; the island is small enough to circle in a day
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU), Mauritius's only international airport

food.name: Dholl puri
food.desc: A thin flatbread stuffed with ground split peas, a beloved everyday street-food staple.

food.name: Rougaille
food.desc: A tomato-based Creole sauce, often cooked with fish, sausage, or eggs and served over rice.

food.name: Mine frite
food.desc: Stir-fried noodles reflecting the island's Chinese-Mauritian culinary influence.

food.name: Alouda
food.desc: A sweet, colorful drink made with milk, basil seeds, and agar jelly.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Mauritius?
faq.a: Not for most nationalities for stays up to 60–90 days, depending on your passport.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International (MRU), the island's only international airport.

faq.q: Do I need to rent a car?
faq.a: Helpful but not essential — taxis are widely available and many resorts also arrange excursions directly.

faq.q: Is Mauritius good for a honeymoon or just families?
faq.a: Both, genuinely — the island has everything from adults-only luxury resorts to family-friendly lagoons, so it comes down to which resort area you choose.

daysReason: 7 days covers the south coast, Chamarel, Grand Bassin, and the east coast at an easy island pace. 4–5 works for a shorter beach-focused trip; 9–10 lets you add the north coast or slow down considerably.
visa: Not required for most nationalities for stays up to 60–90 days — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Le Morne Brabant
attractions.desc: Uma montanha basáltica dramática erguendo-se abruptamente na costa sudoeste da ilha, classificada pela UNESCO pela sua história como refúgio para escravos fugidos. A lagoa circundante é também lar de uma famosa ilusão ótica, uma 'cascata' subaquática visível do ar onde a areia desce da plataforma. É uma das vistas mais fotografadas do país.

attractions.name: Chamarel, Terras das Sete Cores
attractions.desc: Um pequeno local geológico onde o solo vulcânico assentou em faixas distintas de vermelho, castanho e roxo que nunca se misturam, mesmo depois da chuva. Situa-se perto de uma cascata marcante do mesmo nome e de uma destilaria de rum conhecida. A combinação torna-a uma excursão fácil de meio dia a partir da costa.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional das Gargantas do Rio Negro
attractions.desc: A maior área de floresta nativa da ilha, cortada por trilhos que atravessam gargantas íngremes e passam por várias cascatas. É um dos poucos lugares para ver as aves endémicas das Maurícias, várias das quais foram salvas do limiar da extinção. Os trilhos vão desde miradouros fáceis a caminhadas de dia inteiro.

attractions.name: Île aux Cerfs
attractions.desc: Uma pequena ilha na costa leste, alcançável apenas de barco, rodeada de água turquesa e areia branca. Está preparada para um dia inteiro de natação, desportos aquáticos e uma ronda de golfe no seu campo. Os passeios de barco até lá param muitas vezes numa cascata pelo caminho.

attractions.name: Mercado Central de Port Louis
attractions.desc: O mercado coberto da capital é o melhor lugar para ver de perto a mistura cultural da ilha, das bancas de especiarias à comida de rua crioula. Perto dali, o Caudan Waterfront acrescenta uma zona de compras e restauração à beira-mar mais sofisticada. É uma paragem útil para sentir a vida quotidiana para lá dos resorts.

attractions.name: Grand Bassin
attractions.desc: Um lago de cratera considerado um dos locais hindus mais sagrados fora da Índia, rodeado de templos e uma imponente estátua de Shiva visível da estrada abaixo. Atrai grandes multidões de peregrinação durante o festival Maha Shivaratri, mas é tranquilo e contemplativo na maioria dos outros dias. O cenário, nas terras altas arborizadas da ilha, acrescenta ao ambiente.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Costa sul e Le Morne
itinerary.desc: Instala-te perto de Le Morne, com tempo para a lagoa e vistas costeiras.

itinerary.label: Dia 3
itinerary.title: Chamarel e Gargantas do Rio Negro
itinerary.desc: As terras coloridas, uma cascata, e uma caminhada por floresta nativa.

itinerary.label: Dia 4
itinerary.title: Grand Bassin
itinerary.desc: Um desvio cultural para o interior, até ao lago sagrado da cratera.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Costa leste e Île aux Cerfs
itinerary.desc: Praia e um passeio de barco até à pequena ilha ao largo.

itinerary.label: Dia 7
itinerary.title: Port Louis
itinerary.desc: O mercado e o waterfront da capital antes da partida.
itinerary.logistics: ~45min de carro desde a costa leste

goodToKnow.tipping: 10% é apreciado mas não obrigatório; muitos resorts já incluem taxa de serviço
goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro para visitantes, incluindo viajantes sozinhos e famílias
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Carros alugados e táxis funcionam bem; a ilha é pequena o suficiente para dar a volta num dia
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport (MRU), Mauritius's only international airport

food.name: Dholl puri
food.desc: Um pão fino recheado com ervilha partida moída, um clássico de rua muito apreciado.

food.name: Rougaille
food.desc: Um molho crioulo à base de tomate, muitas vezes cozinhado com peixe, salsicha ou ovos e servido com arroz.

food.name: Mine frite
food.desc: Noodles salteados que refletem a influência culinária sino-mauriciana da ilha.

food.name: Alouda
food.desc: Uma bebida doce e colorida feita com leite, sementes de manjericão e gelatina de ágar.
